BACKGROUND: commit 7345632d let an authored handoff be accepted beyond the model-visible candidate cap (projection.candidates is capped at 4; projection.reveal_universe is the full eligible set). SelectedRevealResolver.resolve (validation.py ~198-213) accepts a selected id outside projection.candidates when it equals `authored_handoff_id` and is in reveal_universe. The provider's authored_handoff_id() (cloudflare.py ~310) returns the id of self.authored_handoff, which is set from TWO sources: (1) uniquely_matched_authored_handoff, an exact match on authored wording (cloudflare.py ~341); (2) _semantic_authored_handoff (cloudflare.py ~447-517), where a language model (Jev) answers yes/no on a shortlist of up to 6 eligible candidates, also used as a fallback after an exact TIE (~346). Both get the same beyond-cap privilege. That is wrong: an exact unique authored match is trustworthy; a language-model guess is not.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR (decided by the project owner, option 1):
1. Only a UNIQUE EXACT authored match may be accepted beyond projection.candidates. Add a source marker to AuthoredHandoff (candidate_matcher.py), e.g. `source: Literal["exact","semantic"]`, set where each is built (candidate_matcher.py ~125 exact; cloudflare.py ~517 semantic). authored_handoff_id() must return the id for the beyond-cap exception ONLY when source == "exact". Keep the field default safe (an unmarked handoff must NOT get the privilege).
2. A semantic handoff (including one resolved after an exact tie) must never cause a lost turn: it may only be used if its candidate is inside projection.candidates (what the model can see). Preferred: restrict the semantic shortlist to candidates inside projection.candidates; otherwise discard a semantic pick that falls outside them and record a clear outcome in last_reveal_selection. It must never reach the resolver and raise ineligible_selection. State your choice and the effect on the 6-wide shortlist in the notes.
3. An exact TIE still commits nothing by exact match (existing behaviour); the semantic fallback after a tie is subject to rule 2.
4. Stale state: self.authored_handoff must be cleared on every path where a turn fails or is rolled back, and at the start of every prompt assembly, so a rejected turn's handoff can never carry into the next turn when the provider object is reused. Find where state is restored after a failed turn (engine.py turn loop and the provider) and make the clear explicit.
5. A narrator/model reply must still be unable to set the marker (model selections on handoff turns are already stripped, cloudflare.py ~1708; keep that). Explain in the notes why a model reply cannot set `source`.
6. Do not change what the model sees in its prompt, delivery text, validation of grounding/content/effects, or the one-selection-per-turn rule. No story-specific branches.

TESTS (hermetic, no network; imperative player input per docs/player-input-guide.md; add to tests/test_established_reveal_match.py and reuse its fixtures): (a) exact unique match on a reveal beyond the cap still commits (existing test must keep passing); (b) a SEMANTIC match (stub the semantic_ask callable to answer yes for exactly one candidate that is beyond the cap) does not produce ineligible_selection and does not commit that beyond-cap reveal; a semantic match inside the cap still works; (c) an exact TIE between two reveals, with a stubbed semantic answer picking one beyond the cap, commits nothing beyond the cap and raises no error; (d) FORGED JSON: a model reply that selects a beyond-cap id (with and without an authored handoff on the turn) still raises ineligible_selection or is stripped as today; (e) PROVIDER REUSE: after a turn is rejected (e.g. a guard rejection), the same provider object on the next turn has authored_handoff_id() None until a new match sets it, and a model selection of the previous turn's id is rejected. Name tests so the words semantic, tie, forged and reuse/stale appear in them. Each new test must FAIL on the current code where it exercises the defect (say in the notes which ones did).
